question: What does it cost to rebuild Lumo's four simplest components — button, switch, checkbox, toggle — on Base UI without changing the public API, and what does Base UI fail to express?
verdict: The rebuild is CHEAP TO COMPILE and EXPENSIVE TO SEE. All four components typecheck, keep every exported name and prop name, keep their required announced strings, and emit correct Persian accessible names and roles with zero English. What does not survive is the STYLING CONTRACT: Lumo's cva files address state through React Aria's data-attribute vocabulary, and Base UI's vocabulary differs in NAME (data-checked, not data-selected), in MEANING (data-pressed is the persistent ON state, not the transient pointer-down one), in LOCATION (state lands on the control, not on the wrapping group the `group-*` utilities read), and in COVERAGE (no data-hovered and no data-focus-visible at all — Base UI expects the CSS pseudo-classes). Reusing the variants unchanged, as the brief requires, therefore yields a switch that is correct to a screen reader and frozen on screen, a checkbox whose tick never appears, and a toggle that looks identical on and off. Not one of those is a compile error, and only ONE of the eight is caught by a shipped test — because Lumo has no switch.test.tsx and no checkbox.test.tsx to catch the other two. Cost in source: the four files grew from 580 to 1077 lines (+86%), and 316 lines of that is a new shared adapter plus per-file prop translation that exists only to keep the API still.

how_verified: Every exported name is unchanged: Button, IconButton, buttonVariants, ButtonProps, IconButtonProps, ButtonVariantProps; Switch, switchVariants, switchTrackVariants, switchThumbVariants, SwitchProps, SwitchVariantProps; Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, checkboxVariants, checkboxIndicatorVariants, CheckboxProps, CheckboxGroupProps; Toggle, IconToggle, toggleVariants, ToggleProps, IconToggleProps, ToggleVariantProps. packages/ui/src/index.ts is untouched.

Every prop interface still extends the React Aria type it extended before (Omit<AriaButtonProps,…>, Omit<AriaSwitchFieldProps,…>, Omit<AriaCheckboxFieldProps,…>, Omit<AriaCheckboxGroupProps,…>, Omit<AriaToggleButtonProps,…>), so callers keep isSelected / defaultSelected / isDisabled / isInvalid / onPress / onChange verbatim. Nothing in apps/website or packages/ui was edited to accommodate the swap.
`pnpm --filter @lumo-ui/ui exec tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors in button.tsx, switch.tsx, checkbox.tsx, toggle.tsx, base-ui-adapter.ts, table.tsx and form.tsx.

The four .variants/cva definitions are byte-identical to the baseline: button.variants.ts and toggle.variants.ts are untouched files; switch.tsx's and checkbox.tsx's inline cva blocks were copied across unchanged (verified against experiments/baseline-rac/).
the_constraint.note: No test file was modified, weakened or skipped. The one failure below is reported as data.

method.vendored_from: https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/base-vega/<name>.json — all four returned HTTP 200; raw emit kept in experiments/vendor-base-vega/. scripts/vendor-from-shadcn.mjs targets aria-vega, so base-vega was fetched directly as the brief specifies.
method.baseline: experiments/baseline-rac/<name>.tsx, verified byte-identical to the pre-swap packages/ui/src/<name>.tsx before any edit (diff -q, all four SAME).
probes: experiments/harness/probe.rebuild-simple.test.tsx → experiments/measurements/probe.rebuild-simple.json (rendered DOM + SSR bytes for all four, under fa-IR)
method.probes_live_outside_packages_ui_src: Deliberate: a `vitest run` with no path argument — CI's, or a sibling agent's — must not pick up an experiment's probe. Each carries its own three-line copy/run/rm recipe.
method.not_run: pnpm verify and next build, per the brief (RAM).

size.note: `code` excludes blank lines and lines whose first non-space character starts a comment. Lumo files are comment-heavy by policy, so `code` is the honest comparison and `total` is what a reviewer scrolls.

new_shared_file.why: React Aria → Base UI event translation (PressEvent from click, keyboard event augmentation) plus an `attr()` helper that survives exactOptionalPropertyTypes. It has no "use client", so it stays server-callable.
new_shared_file.distribution_cost: Lumo ships by copy-in. On Base UI this module joins the dependency closure of every interactive component, so a consumer copying `button` now copies three files rather than two.

size.where_the_growth_is: Almost none of it is composition. Base UI's markup is the same shape or simpler than React Aria's; the growth is the prop translation. button.tsx destructures 17 React Aria props to forward 5 of them; toggle.tsx 22 to forward 9; switch.tsx 21 to forward 13; checkbox.tsx 22 to forward 15. That destructuring block is the API-preservation tax, and it is the number this experiment exists to produce.

tests.finding: The brief's `pnpm --filter @lumo-ui/ui exec vitest run src/<name>.test.tsx` is runnable for exactly one of the four. Lumo has 27 test files and three of these four components have no suite of their own. Coverage for button is indirect (five suites render it); coverage for checkbox is indirect and NAME-ONLY (data-display.test.tsx, via table.tsx); coverage for switch is ZERO — nothing in packages/ui/src/*.test.tsx imports Switch. That is why two of the three silent style breaks below are invisible to the suite.

button.verdict: 54 pass, 0 fail. sidebar.test.tsx:94 clicks an `IconButton onPress={toggle}` and passes, which is the direct evidence that the click→PressEvent adapter fires.

failures.title: carries `data-selected` for the ON state, not `data-pressed`
failures.why_left_failing: Emitting a synthetic data-selected would be faking parity. The attribute Base UI emits is the truth, and the test is the measurement.

toggle.note: The SECOND assertion in that same test — `expect(button.hasAttribute("data-pressed")).toBe(false)` — would also have failed; it is never reached because the first throws. So the test pins one defect and would have pinned two.

switch.verdict: UNTESTED. No suite in packages/ui/src imports Switch, so the swap produced 0 pass and 0 fail. The dead-selector breaks below were found by probe, not by test.

checkbox.verdict: 18 pass, 0 fail — and the suite is green while the component's selection wiring is dead. data-display.test.tsx grades accessible NAMES and English leakage in the served bytes, both of which survive the swap. See capability gap `rac_slot_context`.

contamination.warning: This working tree is shared. A SIBLING AGENT is concurrently rebuilding dialog.tsx, popover.tsx and select.tsx on Base UI on the same branch, and those files currently have their own tsc errors. Their failures must not be attributed to this brief.
attribution_evidence: The five failures are all overlay-shape: missing aria-labelledby on role=alertdialog, the two 'Dismiss' sentinels React Aria emits and Base UI does not, and a missing data-has-submenu on MenuItem. None of those attributes is produced by button, switch, checkbox or toggle.
alert-dialog.test.tsx's 'tone=critical puts the destructive variant on the CONFIRM verb only' PASSES, so Button renders and is queryable by its Persian name inside the sibling's dialog.

The remaining question — whether the failing 'cancel closes' test is my onPress adapter or their dialog — is settled by sidebar.test.tsx:94, which clicks an IconButton's onPress and passes. The press fires; the dialog does not close.

At 20:58 a run of button-group + alert-dialog + command + hydrated + overlays with button.tsx ALREADY rebuilt was 32 pass / 0 fail. The five failures appeared only after the sibling's dialog/popover/select edits landed in the tree.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria and Base UI use the SAME attribute name for OPPOSITE concepts, so the styling toggle.variants.ts explicitly warns against is now the correct styling.
capability_gaps.react_aria: data-selected = ON (persistent); data-pressed = pointer is down (transient)
capability_gaps.base_ui: data-pressed = ON (persistent); there is no data-selected and no transient attribute at all
evidence: node_modules/@base-ui/react/toggle/ToggleDataAttributes.d.ts — `pressed = "data-pressed"`, documented "Present when the toggle button is pressed"

Rendered `<Toggle defaultSelected>`: `<button type="button" data-pressed="" tabindex="0" aria-pressed="true" data-lumo="" class="… data-selected:bg-surface-sunken …">` — the class is present, the attribute is not (experiments/measurements/probe.rebuild-simple.json → toggle.on_html)
toggle.variants.ts's own header: "Styling the first is the copy/paste error from a plain Button, and it fails silently: … a toggle that is on looks exactly like a toggle that is off."
capability_gaps.consequence: Every data-selected: utility in toggle.variants.ts is dead. A toggle that is on is visually identical to one that is off.

capability_gaps.claim: Base UI emits no data-hovered and no data-focus-visible on any of the four. It expects the CSS pseudo-classes instead.
evidence: Full attribute census of a rendered `<Button>`: button[class], button[data-lumo], button[tabindex], button[type] — nothing else (probe.rebuild-simple.json → button.attributes)

The data-attribute enums ship the complete list and neither name appears: ButtonDataAttributes has only `disabled`; ToggleDataAttributes only `pressed` and `disabled`; SwitchRootDataAttributes and CheckboxRootDataAttributes have checked/unchecked/indeterminate/disabled/readonly/required/valid/invalid/touched/dirty/filled/focused — `focused`, never `focus-visible`.
shadcn's own base-vega button styles hover as `hover:bg-primary/80` and focus as `focus-visible:ring-3`, i.e. pseudo-classes, confirming this is Base UI's intended idiom rather than an omission.
capability_gaps.consequence: No hover feedback on any of the four, and no focus ring on switch or checkbox. FOCUS_RING in form.tsx exists precisely because those two controls hide their focusable <input>; on Base UI it produces no ring at all, which is a WCAG 2.4.7 failure rather than a cosmetic one.
capability_gaps.caught_by: nothing. No shipped test asserts a hover or focus-visible attribute on these components.

capability_gaps.claim: Even where a state attribute exists under a different name, it is on the WRONG ELEMENT for Lumo's `group-*` utilities. React Aria puts the state on the wrapping <label> (the `group`); Base UI puts it on the control itself, which is a SIBLING of, or the very element bearing, the utility that wants to read it.
evidence: Rendered `<Switch defaultSelected>`: `data-checked` sits on the role=switch <span> (the track) and on the thumb <span>; the wrapping <label class="group …"> carries only data-filled. (probe.rebuild-simple.json → switch.html)

Rendered `<Checkbox defaultSelected>`: `data-checked` sits on the role=checkbox <span> (the box). The two <svg> marks INSIDE it still read `group-data-selected:block`, whose nearest `.group` ancestor is the label — which has no such attribute. (probe.rebuild-simple.json → checkbox.mark_classes)
has_data_selected_anywhere: false / has_data_checked_anywhere: true, for both components.
capability_gaps.consequence: Two independent reasons the same rule cannot fire: wrong name AND wrong ancestor. Switch: the track never fills and the thumb never leaves its resting inset — the switch is visually frozen. Checkbox: both marks keep `hidden` in every state, so a ticked checkbox shows an empty box.
capability_gaps.note: Base UI's own answer for the checkbox is <Checkbox.Indicator>, which mounts conditionally. Adopting it means rewriting the icon class strings, which is a restyle; this experiment swaps the engine only. Recorded rather than done.
capability_gaps.caught_by: nothing. There is no switch.test.tsx and no checkbox.test.tsx.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria's `slot` is a NAME in a parent's context map; Base UI has no context-injection mechanism, so `slot` can only be the native web-components attribute. `<Checkbox slot="selection">` therefore stops selecting.
evidence: table.tsx:380 and :400 render `<Checkbox slot="selection" aria-label={label} />`, and its header at :80 documents the wiring.

React Aria types it `slot?: string | null` (null = opt out of the parent's context). The DOM attribute is `string | undefined` and cannot express null; tsc reports `Type 'null' is not assignable to type 'string | undefined'`.

MEASURED, experiments/measurements/probe.table-selection.json: clicking the select-all checkbox in a `selectionMode="multiple"` table moves its own aria-checked to "true" and leaves every row's aria-selected at "false". selection_propagated: false.
capability_gaps.consequence: Every selectable table in the library renders correctly-named, correctly-Persian, entirely inert checkboxes.
capability_gaps.caught_by: nothing. data-display.test.tsx passes 18/18 across this defect, because it grades accessible names and English leakage rather than wiring.

capability_gaps.claim: Base UI ships no press or hover abstraction, so eight React Aria handlers are accepted by the unchanged public API and never fire.

onPress.implemented_as: onClick, with a PressEvent built field-by-field from the real click (base-ui-adapter.ts → pressFromClick)
onPress.works: Verified by sidebar.test.tsx:94, which clicks an IconButton's onPress and passes.
not_recoverable: pointerType: a click is a MouseEvent, so touch and pen are indistinguishable from mouse. `detail === 0` → "virtual" is React Aria's own rule for keyboard/AT activation and is reproduced; a TOUCH press is reported as "mouse", and a caller branching on pointerType === "touch" silently takes the wrong branch.
key: React Aria reports Space vs Enter here. A click carries neither, so the field is omitted rather than filled with a plausible value.
continuePropagation(): a no-op. Base UI never stopped propagation, so there is nothing to resume.

press-and-drag-off cancellation: React Aria cancels a press when the pointer leaves the target before release; a click does not fire in that case either, so this one happens to agree — but by the platform's rule, not by a mechanism Lumo controls.

capability_gaps.faked_note: The PressEvent is built only from fields the DOM event actually carries. Nothing is invented; the fields that cannot be derived are listed above rather than filled in.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria's `isPending` disables press and hover while keeping focusability AND announces the pending state to a screen reader. Base UI has no counterpart.
capability_gaps.evidence: ButtonProps in @base-ui/react/button is NativeButtonProps + BaseUIComponentProps + `focusableWhenDisabled`. There is no pending prop, no data-pending attribute in ButtonDataAttributes, and no live region anywhere in the button implementation.
capability_gaps.consequence: The prop is accepted and does nothing. A caller who used it gets a button that stays fully interactive with no announcement.
capability_gaps.note: No current Lumo or website call site passes isPending (grep: 0 occurrences), so nothing regressed today. It is a promise the type still makes.

capability_gaps.claim: React Aria's `validationBehavior: 'native' | 'aria'` has no Base UI equivalent, and its absence reopens the exact defect form.tsx exists to prevent.
evidence: form.tsx's Form header: `validationBehavior` defaults to "aria" deliberately, because native constraint validation renders the BROWSER's message in the BROWSER UI language — "a Persian page opened in an English-chrome browser therefore shows an English error under a Persian label".
Base UI's nearest prop is Field.Root's `validationMode: 'onSubmit' | 'onBlur' | 'onChange'`, which is a different axis: WHEN to validate, not WHETHER the browser owns the message.
experiments/measurements/base-ui-i18n.json already recorded the underlying fact: field/root/useFieldValidation.mjs:201 reads `element.validationMessage`, so the message language follows the browser.
capability_gaps.consequence: There is no setting that turns native validation copy off. The English-error-under-a-Persian-label defect has no switch to flip.

capability_gaps.claim: Both libraries expose a `render` prop and they are not the same prop; the compiler says so.
capability_gaps.evidence: tsc TS2322 on Button: `Type 'DOMRenderFunction<"button", ButtonRenderProps>' is not assignable … Type 'ButtonState' is missing the following properties from type 'ButtonRenderProps': isHovered, isPressed, isFocused, isFocusVisible, and 2 more`. React Aria hands the callback six state flags; Base UI hands it one (`disabled`).
capability_gaps.consequence: `render` is accepted by the unchanged type and dropped. This is the one gap the type system announces rather than hides.

gaps.note: Base UI spreads Root props to the visible <span>, not to the hidden <input> that is actually focusable, so autoFocus lands on a non-focusable element. Dropped rather than placed somewhere it would not work.
same reason. On button and toggle it IS expressible and is translated to tabIndex={-1}.
Base UI's CheckboxGroup has `disabled` and no read-only concept; neither does Field.Root.
no group-level required in Base UI.

React Aria types it `Key` (string | number) because in a ToggleButtonGroup it doubles as the selection key. Base UI types it `string`. A numeric id is stringified, which the DOM would do anyway; a group could no longer round-trip it as a number.
both libraries accept a callback, but React Aria's takes its render props and Base UI's takes its own state. Dropped rather than called with the wrong argument.
TRANSLATED, not dropped. React Aria returns `string | string[] | true | null | undefined` where `true` means VALID; Base UI returns `string | string[] | null`. The wrapper maps true/undefined → null.

capability_gaps.claim: This one is React Aria's defect, found by the swap. ToggleButtonProps declares `Omit<GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, 'onClick'>` for a component that renders a <button>.
capability_gaps.evidence: tsc: `Type 'BaseUIEvent<MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>>' is not assignable to type 'MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>' … Property 'align' is missing in type 'EventTarget & HTMLButtonElement'`. ButtonProps, by contrast, uses GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> and needed no cast.
capability_gaps.consequence: toggle.tsx carries one `as object` cast on the passthrough bag; button.tsx carries none.

english_strings.question: Any English string Base UI emits that no prop reaches, in these four components?
measured: Switch with isInvalid + errorMessage, SSR under fa-IR: invalid_ssr_english = []
CheckboxGroup with two Checkboxes, SSR under fa-IR: group_ssr_english = []
english_strings.why: These four are the components with no library-authored copy in either engine. React Aria leaked nothing here either; its 8 measured leaks live in Table, ComboBox, NumberField, Calendar and the overlays. Base UI's 8, per experiments/measurements/base-ui-i18n.json, live in NumberField, Slider, Combobox and Autocomplete. This batch is the intersection where both libraries are silent, which is exactly why it was the right batch to swap first — and why it produces no i18n signal at all.

improvement_found.what: React Aria's Table injects `Select All` and `Select` into the selection checkboxes, which table.tsx overrides with Persian aria-labels. On Base UI those strings never exist to override.
improvement_found.caveat: Not a win: the same change is what killed the selection wiring (gap `rac_slot_context`). The English went away because the mechanism went away.

what_survived_untouched: The required announced strings. IconButton.label, IconToggle.label and CheckboxGroup.label are still required `string`, and they still land: `aria-label="حذف"`, `aria-label="بی‌صدا"`, and a role=group whose aria-labelledby resolves to «کانال‌های اطلاع‌رسانی» (probe.rebuild-simple.json → checkbox.group.resolved_name). This is the part of Lumo the primitive never provided, so no primitive could take it away — the clearest single result in this measurement.
Roles and ARIA state: role=switch + aria-checked, role=checkbox + aria-checked, role=group + aria-labelledby, aria-pressed on the toggle, all correct.

Description and error wiring: Base UI's Field.Root/Field.Description gives the switch's <span role=switch> an aria-describedby pointing at the help text (probe: description_wired = true), which is the job RAC's <Text slot="description"> did.
Logical utilities: every reused class string is unchanged, so the RTL rules hold; button-group.test.tsx's byte-equal-class-set-under-rtl-and-ltr assertion still passes.

LumoNode on children, data-lumo on every root, and the cva-lives-in-*.variants.ts split (button.variants.ts and toggle.variants.ts are untouched; base-ui-adapter.ts deliberately carries no "use client").
limitations: SHARED WORKING TREE. dialog.tsx, popover.tsx and select.tsx were rebuilt by a sibling agent during this session and currently fail tsc. The five alert-dialog/overlays failures are theirs; the attribution evidence is listed under tests.contamination, but it is inference from failure shape plus one timing observation, not from a clean-room re-run.

NO VISUAL VERIFICATION. Every dead-selector claim is derived from the rendered class list and the rendered attribute set — the class is present, the attribute is absent, therefore the rule cannot match. No browser rendered these components and no screenshot was taken. jsdom does not apply Tailwind.

NO GATE NUMBERS. packages/gate's RULES were not run over these renders, and `pnpm verify` was not run, per the brief. The English counts above come from a regex over spoken attributes and text, not from the real rules.

INTERACTION COVERAGE IS THIN. One real click is exercised (sidebar's IconButton onPress, and the table select-all). Keyboard activation, focus movement, form submission and controlled-value round-trips were not exercised for any of the four.

CHECKBOXGROUP VALUE PLUMBING IS UNTESTED. RAC's onChange(string[]) is mapped to Base UI's onValueChange(string[], details) by first-argument compatibility. The shapes match on paper and no test exercises it.

THE ADAPTER IS A FIFTH FILE. Its 126 lines are counted in the totals, but a decision to adopt Base UI would need to decide whether it is a shared package module or duplicated per copy-in component; that choice changes the number.

upstream_note.why_it_matters: That is a PHYSICAL transform for the thumb's travel. switch.tsx's header devotes a section to why Lumo uses `start-*` (inset-inline-start) instead: translate-x has no logical counterpart, so an ON switch slides toward the reading END in English and back toward the reading START in Persian, silently. shadcn's Base UI switch ships that defect today. It is recorded here because it is the same class of defect this repository's ledger tracks, found in the upstream this experiment vendored from — and Lumo's own class strings, reused unchanged, do not have it.
